title: Development of a dynamic multi-agent network for building energy modeling: A case study towards scalable and autonomous energy modeling
V83_REASON: BEM-AI uses A2A/MCP to automate building-energy-modeling workflows and is validated through case studies/reliability tests. Its effects are modeling/simulation artifacts, not consequential external-world commits requiring runtime decision-validity revalidation.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Energy and Buildings / ScienceDirect publisher abstract

title: ProteinMCP: An agentic AI framework for autonomous protein engineering
V83_REASON: Agent autonomously plans and invokes 38 MCP bioinformatics/protein-engineering tools end-to-end. Demonstrated execution remains computational scientific workflow execution; no consequential physical/clinical action commit or validity gate is established.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Protein Science publisher full text / PMC

title: Agentic AI as a coordination paradigm in digital health and agri-food systems
V83_REASON: Perspective explicitly frames task-bounded agents under institutional/regulatory constraints and MCP as a mechanism for policy, provenance and accountability. Highly relevant governance/mechanism synthesis, but conceptual/perspective evidence rather than a validated primary execution mechanism.

title: Contamination Prevention in Agentic Workflow Assessments
V83_REASON: Architecture prevents evaluation-awareness/data contamination in bias assessments. The protected object is assessment validity, not validity of a consequential external agent decision across a decision-to-effect boundary.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: TU Dublin institutional publication full abstract

title: Energy-limited Lifelong Multi-agent Pickup and Delivery
V83_REASON: Fallback priority planning ensures a feasible action in each concurrent planning/execution episode under energy/collision constraints. This is strong constrained planning for embodied agents, but not LLM/agentic-AI decision-validity revalidation of authority/premises before consequential commit.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Machine Intelligence Research / Springer publisher article

title: Towards Autonomous Personal Health Knowledge Graphs Through Multi-agent Collaboration
V83_REASON: Prototype uses LLM agents/MCP for personal-health knowledge-graph construction and querying. The demonstrated function is information integration/querying, not execution of a consequential health action.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Springer chapter record and author/institutional bibliographic evidence

title: SPAR: Scalable Prioritized Agent Routing for Multi-agent Networks
V83_REASON: SPAR coordinates and prioritizes decentralized inter-agent task/request propagation and interoperates with MCP/A2A/ANP. It is communication/orchestration infrastructure and does not establish a validity gate for consequential action execution.

title: Agent-in-the-Loop: Using AI Agents to Perform Control-Oriented Simulation Tasks
V83_REASON: Study tests whether LLM agents can reliably plan and orchestrate precise multi-step control-oriented simulation toolchains. The execution target is simulation/model-based engineering rather than consequential real-world control.

title: Intelligent Multi-Agent Orchestration Framework for Enterprise Financial Systems
V83_REASON: Framework routes enterprise financial requests among transaction, risk, compliance and advisory agents with confidence-based fallback and MCP interoperability. Abstract evidence does not establish whether transactions are live external commits or whether a validation/authority gate controls them; retain pending.

title: MCP-Diag: A Deterministic, Protocol-Driven Architecture for AI-Native Network Diagnostics
V83_REASON: Architecture provides deterministic grounding and a mandatory protocol-level HITL authorization loop before tool invocation, but demonstrated tools are diagnostic utilities (dig/ping/traceroute), not consequential remediation actions. Strong governance mechanism, non-consequential demonstrated effect.

title: Agentic AI at the 6G Edge: A Blueprint for Proactive and Energy-Aware Resource Allocation
V83_REASON: PRIMAL combines predictive telemetry, adaptive thresholds and capacity-aware admission control for autonomous edge-resource decisions. Prototype evaluation shows operational allocation benefits, but source evidence does not establish explicit runtime revalidation of authority/premises before resource commits.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: IEEE Network / Western Sydney University publication record

title: Towards Fluid Networks: An Agentic AI Framework Using MCP for EBPF Service Orchestration
V83_REASON: Hierarchical agentic framework translates natural-language intents into fine-grained eBPF/network programmability, making consequential network state changes plausible. Recovered abstract evidence is insufficient to determine whether proposed operational plans undergo explicit validity/authority revalidation before deployment.

title: Native MCP Server in Oracle Autonomous AI Database-Enabling High Performance Agentic AI Workloads
V83_REASON: Native MCP exposes schema discovery, SQL execution and agent tools with database security integration and evaluates performance/concurrency. Contribution is secure/high-performance tool access; recovered evidence does not establish decision-validity revalidation governing consequential database mutations.

title: Opportunity Scout: A Modular Explainable Agentic AI System for Autonomous Opportunity Discovery
V83_REASON: Agent autonomously discovers, filters and explains online job/business opportunities. It produces information/recommendations rather than committing consequential external actions.

title: An agentic AI framework connecting language models to electronic health records and a biomedical knowledge graph for real-world evidence
V83_REASON: MedCP uses audited read-only, least-privileged tools and interactive human supervision to execute EHR/KG research queries. Strong access governance is present, but tools are deliberately read-only and the system is a research assistant rather than an executor of consequential clinical actions.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence publisher full text / PMC

title: VASPilot: MCP-facilitated multi-agent intelligence for autonomous VASP simulations
V83_REASON: CrewAI/MCP agents autonomously configure and execute VASP computational-materials workflows. Effects remain scientific simulations/calculations, so the demonstrated system lacks the consequential external decision-to-effect boundary required for CORE.
V83_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Chinese Physics B metadata; VASPilot author repository/preprint

title: MedScrubCrew: A Medical Multi-Agent Framework for Automating Appointment Scheduling Based on Patient-Provider Profile Resource Matching
V83_REASON: Framework automates triage classification and appointment scheduling using matching, knowledge graphs and role-based agents. It is operationally consequential scheduling, but the paper does not establish an execution-time validity/authority revalidation gate before booking/assignment.

title: Agentic RAG Systems for Real-Time Financial Decision Making: A Multi-Agent Framework with Model Context Protocol Integration
V83_REASON: Multi-agent RAG/MCP framework combines market analysis, risk and regulatory-compliance agents and improves prediction/decision latency. Evaluation is on financial datasets/decision support; source evidence does not demonstrate live trade execution governed by a validity-preserving commit gate.

title: LLM and MCP Enabled AI Agent for Autonomous Multi-Lingual Alerts for Coastal Communities
V83_REASON: Source confirms an autonomous MCP/LLM alerting agent for coastal communities, a potentially consequential communication action. Recovered evidence is insufficient to determine trigger validation, authority checks, approval semantics, or whether alerts are actually externally issued in evaluation.

title: ROSBag MCP Server: Analyzing Robot Data with LLMs for Agentic Embodied AI Applications
V83_REASON: MCP server analyzes, visualizes, filters and processes ROS/ROS2 bag data and benchmarks LLM tool calling. It does not control a robot or commit consequential embodied actions.
